searchText: Would recommend reading the code, there are multiple implementation so choose one in the language that you know. If you are in rust, this is main Interpreter loop: https://github.com/bluealloy/revm/blob/main/crates/interpreter/src/interpreter.rs#L238-L240 and it calls instructions (opcode functions) found here: https://github.com/bluealloy/revm/tree/main/crates/interpreter/src/instructions Hello everone. We found BLS12-381 very useful for even more applications. What shall we do to make it available in evm asap after Dencun? Add more implementations, benchmarks, tests? Do you even think it might be worth to activate it? Start with fixing the EIP I think <@539495253418180618> is planning it's revival for the next fork The biggest re-evaluation that the BLS EIP needs is for the gas to be re-costed with up-to-date implementations. My opinion is that the precompile should be costed so that repeated calls of the the keccak/sha3 operation is the most gas efficient way to "waste time" in the EVM, whenever using benchmarks to test. Costing at 35MGas/s (on a typical AWS instance with below-average compute) is an older standard. I think 50MGas/s would be a safer option, although it would increase the gas cost of the precompiles. Opinions lightly held if there is consensus for a different costing. btw i am realizing the variable length encoding may be kind of important for another reason, which is otherwise code sections are fundamentally limited to 64kb (i think <@403707149043105803> may have pointed this out before but i can't remember when) That limits toe total code size to 64megs, in 64k chunks. Hopefully that will take at least 5 years before it matters and we can have an eof2 container format then? Or we can add a new code section type with variable sizing. I do think there are compatible ways to address it on L1 maybe what if some L2 wants to allow people to deploy larger contracts? they would have to break evm compatibility Larger than 64 megs? Or even just 1 meg?
